tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local negative-control replay of the prior abstract claim/idempotency model. Same-run atomic conditional commit semantics are restored: marker absence check, effect:E, and marker creation occur as one indivisible winner transition. Serialized authority turnover and distinct non-reusable authority identities are retained. The single removed assumption is marker persistence across recurrence/crash reconstruction: effect:E remains externally observable after the first successful run, but a later recurring invocation reconstructs local durable state with the marker absent. No public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, external coordinator, richer-mode arbitration, hosted compute, concrete transport, or optional second semantic leaf is modeled.

restored_assumptions: atomic conditional marker-absent check plus effect:E plus marker creation within each invocation
counterexample_schedule: A0 is current; effect:E is not yet recorded and the marker is absent.
Invocation I0 executes one atomic conditional transition: it observes marker absent, performs effect:E, and creates the marker; no same-run competitor can also win.
A later recurrence/crash reconstruction preserves the already-produced external effect:E but reconstructs local state with the marker absent.
Authority advances serially to distinct current identity A1.
Invocation I1 executes the same atomic conditional transition under A1, again observes marker absent, performs effect:E a second time, and recreates the marker.
fixture.duplicate_effect_search: A cross-recurrence duplicate schedule exists even though each individual invocation has perfect atomic conditional commit semantics, because loss of the durable idempotency marker makes the later invocation indistinguishable from a never-executed state.
fixture.authority_check: Current-authority-only execution is preserved: I0 executes under current A0 and I1 executes under current A1 after serialized turnover. The failure is reconstruction/idempotency persistence, not stale-authority execution or same-run race.

observations: Restoring perfect same-run atomicity eliminates the prior two-attempt race but does not prevent a later recurrence from repeating an already-visible effect when its durable marker is lost.
Serialized authority turnover is orthogonal to this failure: both executions can be authority-correct while the effect is duplicated across generations.

For cross-run at-most-once behavior, either the idempotency decision must survive recurrence/crash reconstruction or the effect primitive itself must deduplicate a stable effect identity across runs independently of local marker recovery.
inference: Within this exact abstract model, same-invocation atomic check/effect/marker semantics are insufficient for cross-recurrence at-most-once execution if marker state can disappear while the external effect persists. A recurrence-stable durable idempotency record or behaviorally equivalent external idempotent effect keyed by a stable effect identity is necessary. This does not establish any concrete Chat-exposed transport, storage durability guarantee, crash transaction boundary, fork exclusion, or real multi-claimant implementation.
unresolved_children: A concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent Chat-exposed primitive providing recurrence-stable conditional idempotency remains unverified.
Crash consistency where an external effect commits but local marker persistence fails remains unresolved unless both share one transactional boundary or the effect is independently idempotent.
Fork exclusion and stale-authority behavior remain unverified under loss of serialized authority turnover.

A next negative control should restore atomic commit and marker persistence, then remove serialized authority turnover/fencing to isolate stale-authority execution from duplicate-suppression correctness.
